audit.whatIsWrong: content win[0] reads Wukong while whys[0] says Level 1 is even. win[2] reads Skill while whys[2] and the mid prose both say Level 3 favours Aatrox. win[3] reads Skill while whys[3] says 4-5 tips to Wukong. win[5] reads Skill while whys[5] says first item swings the extended brawl back to your drain.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill, Skill, Aatrox, Wukong, Wukong, Aatrox, Aatrox — which is exactly the shape the prose describes: even start, Aatrox's level-3 window, Wukong's armour-stacking and Cyclone window, then Aatrox from first item on. 50.83% over 3604 games.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-2 even; Level 3 to Aatrox; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 to Wukong; First item and Two+ items to Aatrox.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster and Cyclone are the two abilities the entry tells you to 'play around' and neither has a cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is 22/21/20/19/18 and Cyclone 130/110/90. Twenty-two seconds is an enormous window at rank 1 — a Wukong who has spent the clone has no escape and no target-break for the whole of your next rotation. Crushing Blow is 8s and Nimbus Strike 10s.
audit.corrected: 22s Warrior Trickster and 130s Cyclone written into spikes[1], spikes[3] and mid; 8s Crushing Blow and 10s Nimbus Strike into spikes[0] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster is described only as a clone that 'breaks target'. It also turns Wukong INVISIBLE and dashes him away — the clone is the decoy, the stealth is the escape, and the entry never mentions it. Crushing Blow is described as 'armor shred' without its other half: it extends his attack range, so the auto that shreds you lands from further out than the one you are spacing against.
audit.why: Riot's text: Warrior Trickster — 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone that will attack nearby enemies'; Crushing Blow — 'Wukong's next attack gains attack range, deals bonus damage, and reduces the target's armor for a few seconds.' The stealth is why chasing after the clone fails even when you correctly ignore the decoy, and the extended range is why his trade opens before you think you are in his threat radius.
audit.corrected: Invisibility and the dash named alongside the clone in spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[1]; the attack-range extension on Crushing Blow stated in spikes[0] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stone Skin is called 'passive armor stacks' with no mention of what else it gives him.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Wukong gains stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions and monsters.' It is armour AND health regeneration, and both only build while the fight runs — which means a long brawl feeds him and short repeated trades do not. That reframes the advice from 'force extended brawls' to 'burst in windows'.
audit.corrected: Health regeneration named alongside the armour in spikes[0]; Grievous Wounds implied by naming the regen rather than inventing an item line.

edits.before: Level 3 is your clean window — your Q pattern out-brawls his early trades, so land the third-Q knockup to interrupt his Nimbus Strike (E) dash-in and drain through his passive armor stacks before he spikes.
edits.after: Level 3 is your clean window — knock him up out of Nimbus Strike (10s) and burst before Stone Skin banks armour and health regen, both of which only build while the fight runs. Crushing Blow (8s) also extends his reach.

edits.before: His armor-stacking and level-6 Cyclone (R) tip 4-6 his way; watch his Warrior Trickster (W) clone — it breaks target and dodges your combo, so don't commit onto the decoy, bait the clone and R, then punish the cooldown.
edits.after: His armour stacking and Cyclone (130s) tip 4-6 his way. Warrior Trickster (22s) does not just leave a clone — it turns him invisible and dashes him out, so the decoy is the bait and the stealth is the escape. Punish that 22s.

edits.before: Level 3 favours Aatrox — your Q rotation and drain out-brawl his early burst, and the knockup interrupts his Nimbus Strike engage. But 4-5 and 6 swing to Wukong: his armor stacking, his all-in, and Cyclone (R) beat you, and his Warrior Trickster clone breaks your targeting and dodges your Q sweetspot or R. Never commit your combo onto the decoy. Bait the clone, punish the cooldown, and re-spike hard at your first item where you take the brawl back.
edits.after: Level 3 favours Aatrox — the knockup interrupts Nimbus Strike (10s) and your rotation beats his burst. But 4-5 and 6 swing to Wukong: Stone Skin banks armour and health regen the longer a fight runs, and Cyclone (130s) knocks you out of yours. Warrior Trickster (22s) makes him invisible and dashes him clear while the clone holds your target — never commit onto the decoy. Punish that 22s, and re-spike at first item.

edits.before: Dodge your Q sweetspot and R by cloning with Warrior Trickster
edits.after: Go invisible on W and dash out while the clone holds you

edits.before: Wukong changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Wukong clone, E, armor shred, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Wukong wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Wukong changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Warrior Trickster (W, 22s), which turns him invisible and dashes him out while a clone holds the target, and a Crushing Blow that extends his attack range as it shreds armour. Aatrox wins by spacing against that longer reach, refusing to commit onto the decoy, and bursting before Stone Skin banks armour and regen through a long fight.

edits.before: Wukong clone, E, armor shred, and R
edits.after: W: clone plus invisible dash out

notes: Wukong's kit lives at champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json, not wukong.json — anything iterating enemy slugs by display name will miss him. There is also a separate champ-data/_kits/jadewukong.json in the same directory; I used monkeyking.json, which is the Data Dragon id for the Wukong in this matchup. Worth confirming which of the two the site's slug mapping resolves to.
